findings.summary: Part 2 teaches the composite patterns (fan-out, fan-in) on pages 1–2 and only afterwards teaches the three primitives they are built from — closing rules, select, and nil channels — inverting the syllabus order (chapters 5–7 land after chapters 8–9).
findings.evidence: Page order is: 1 "Fan-Out: Spreading Work", 2 "Fan-In: Merging N Channels", 3 "Merge Leaks And Who Closes" ("THE RULE: only a sender closes..."), 4 "Channel Or Mutex, And select Basics" ("select In One Screen"), 5 "Timeouts And select Edge Cases", 6 "nil Channels And The Decision Guide". The syllabus orders these as Closing Channels (ch5) → select (ch6) → nil Channels (ch7) → Fan-Out (ch8) → Fan-In (ch9) → Cheat Sheet (ch10).
findings.fix: Reorder Part 2 to close → select → nil → fan-out → fan-in → gotchas/cheat sheet: move current pages 3's "Who Closes" section, 4's select material and 5–6 ahead of the two pattern pages, leaving the leak/cheat-sheet material last.

findings.summary: The caption's topic list describes Part 1 material (unbuffered rendezvous, buffer sizing, hchan internals) rather than the fan-out/fan-in/select/nil-channel pages this part actually contains.
findings.evidence: Caption: "These ten pages are the whole channel model: unbuffered rendezvous, buffer sizing that is a memory ceiling rather than a perf knob, the hchan fast path, the three ways close panics, and the nil-channel trick" — but the six page titles are "Fan-Out: Spreading Work", "Fan-In: Merging N Channels", "Merge Leaks And Who Closes", "Channel Or Mutex, And select Basics", "Timeouts And select Edge Cases", "nil Channels And The Decision Guide"; no page covers hchan internals or buffer sizing as a memory ceiling.
findings.fix: Rewrite the topic list to match this part: "fan-out worker pools and picking N, the general fan-in merge, the two goroutine leaks and who is allowed to close, channel vs mutex, select timeouts and edge cases, and the nil-channel trick that turns select into a switchboard."

findings.summary: `select` is used as the cancellation idiom on page 1 but its semantics are not introduced until page 4.
findings.evidence: Page 1 code: "select {","case results <- r: // normal path","case <-ctx.Done(): return // no leak". Page 4 first introduces it: "select waits on many channel operations at once" / "Several ready? It picks one uniformly at random".
findings.fix: Move the "select In One Screen" section (and the nil/closed select table) ahead of the fan-out page, or at minimum precede the guarded-send snippet with the one-line definition of what select does.

findings.summary: The caption states a page count that does not match the deck.
findings.evidence: Caption says "These ten pages"; the part has 6 slides (page_title entries in data/handbooks/go/channels/parts/02/post.json).
findings.fix: Change "These ten pages" to "These six pages".

findings.summary: The caption opens with a series label instead of a hook, burying the actual hook in the second sentence.
findings.evidence: First sentence: "Part 2 of GO CHANNELS: FIELD NOTES."
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and move the label after it: "Most Go concurrency bugs are not race conditions — they are one goroutine parked forever on a send nobody will ever receive. Part 2 of GO CHANNELS: FIELD NOTES."

findings.summary: Two code lines are clipped at the right edge of their code blocks, cutting off the trailing comments mid-word.
findings.evidence: Block 1 renders `go worker(jobs, results) // one chai` (truncated from "one channel"); block 2 renders `err error // one chan, sane orderin` (truncated from "ordering").
findings.fix: Shorten these inline comments to fit the code-block width (e.g. `// one chan` and `// sane order`), or enable wrapping/reduce the code font size so the full line renders inside the block.

findings.summary: Page 1 asserts close's broadcast behaviour and closes `jobs` to terminate workers, but the closing rules and the broadcast property are only established on pages 3 and 4.
findings.evidence: Page 1: "One `close(jobs)` terminates all N workers" / "A close broadcasts to every blocked receiver at once". Page 3: "THE RULE: only a sender closes, and only if it is solo". Page 4: "Closing wakes every goroutine blocked on receive" / "That broadcast is how one `done` cancels N workers".
findings.fix: Place the Closing Channels material (who closes, the closer goroutine, the broadcast property, the panic table) before the fan-out page so `close(jobs)` is a use of a taught rule rather than an assertion.

findings.summary: A select-case line in the "The General Merge" code block is clipped at the right edge, cutting the comment mid-word.
findings.evidence: `case out ← v: // consumer still readin` — the trailing "g" of "reading" is cut off at the block boundary.
findings.fix: Trim the comment to `// consumer reads` so the line fits inside the code block width.

findings.summary: The "General Merge" section shows only the setup lines and never the merge goroutines or the closer, so the canonical merge is split across the page and page 3.
findings.evidence: Page 2 "The General Merge" code is only "var wg sync.WaitGroup","wg.Add(len(cs))","out := make(chan T, len(cs))", followed by the bare claim "The `wg.Wait()` closer goroutine is mandatory"; the per-input goroutine loop appears only at the bottom under "The Loop Var Trap", and the closer body `go func(){ wg.Wait(); close(out) }()` only on page 3.
findings.fix: Put the full canonical merge — wg setup, the per-input goroutine loop, and the `go func(){ wg.Wait(); close(out) }()` closer — in one code block under "The General Merge", and let the later "Loop Var Trap" section annotate the capture rather than first reveal the loop.

findings.summary: The closer-goroutine code block clips its comment at the right edge, ending mid-word.
findings.evidence: `close(out) // after N producers fin:` — truncated from "finish"/"finished".
findings.fix: Shorten the comment to `// after N producers done` so it fits within the code block.

findings.summary: The nil-out fix `a = nil` is shown as code before the busy-spin bug it repairs is ever stated; the problem statement appears two pages later.
findings.evidence: Page 4 ends with "if !ok { a = nil; continue }" / "// loop while a != nil || b != nil" with no surrounding explanation. Page 6 opens with the missing premise: "A closed input stays ready and busy-spins the loop" / "Nil the variable and select drops that case for good".
findings.fix: Move the two page-6 opening bullets (closed case stays ready → busy spin) onto page 4 immediately above that snippet, and introduce `a`/`b` as the two merge inputs so "loop while a != nil || b != nil" and page 6's "Both inputs nil?" have an antecedent.
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: The caption claims the set is ten pages and lists Part 1 topics, but this part has six pages and covers none of those topics.
findings.evidence: "These ten pages are the whole channel model: unbuffered rendezvous, buffer sizing ..., the hchan fast path, the three ways close panics, and the nil-channel trick" — this part has 6 slides (Fan-Out, Fan-In, Merge Leaks, Channel Or Mutex, Timeouts, nil Channels), and unbuffered rendezvous / buffer sizing / hchan are in Part 1 (9 pages).
findings.fix: Rewrite the Part 2 caption to its own page count and subject matter, e.g. "These six pages cover fan-out/fan-in, who closes, the two goroutine leaks, channel-vs-mutex, and select's nil-channel switchboard."

findings.summary: The closing flow diagram names a "fan-in merge" stage one page before fan-in is defined.
findings.evidence: Page 1 diagram spec nodes: ["generator","fan-out workers","fan-in merge","consumer"]; page 2 first defines it: "Fan-in: N input channels merged into one output".
findings.fix: Move the pipeline flow diagram to the end of page 2, where "Pipeline Contract" already discusses the chained stages.

findings.summary: The unconditional bullet telling readers to capture the loop variable is outdated for Go 1.22+ and contradicts the page's own later bullet.
findings.evidence: "Capture the loop variable or all goroutines share one" appears as a present-tense rule, while the same page later says "Pre-Go 1.22 the goroutines all shared one `c`" — since Go 1.22 the `for ... range` variable is per-iteration, so no capture is required.
findings.fix: Reword to a version-scoped statement, e.g. "Pre-Go 1.22: capture `c` or all goroutines share one" (or "Passing `c` in is still the portable shape"), so it no longer reads as a current requirement.

findings.summary: Page 3 ends with an unheaded non-blocking-receive select snippet while page 4 opens with three closing-channel bullets, so the two blocks sit under the wrong topics on either side of the page break.
findings.evidence: Page 3's final block is "select {","case v := <-ch: use(v)","default: // nothing ready, move on" placed after the "Who Closes" section with no heading or prose; page 4's first block is "Buffered values survive a close; receivers drain first" / "Closing wakes every goroutine blocked on receive".
findings.fix: Swap them: keep the three close bullets with the "Who Closes" section on page 3, and move the non-blocking receive snippet into page 4's "select In One Screen" section beside the non-blocking send example it pairs with.

findings.summary: `select {}` is used as a known form on page 5 but is only defined on page 6.
findings.evidence: Page 5: "With no `default:` that is just `select {}` in disguise". Page 6: "`select {}` with no cases parks that goroutine forever".
findings.fix: Move the "`select {}` with no cases parks that goroutine forever" line into page 5's "select Edge Cases" list, ahead of the all-nil comparison.

findings.summary: The `select {}` parking fact is filed under the "Guard Every Send" heading, which is about pairing sends with `ctx.Done()`.
findings.evidence: Page 6 "Guard Every Send" bullets: "An unguarded `out <- v` is the **#1** source of leaks" followed by "`select {}` with no cases parks that goroutine forever" and "Nil a local variable, never a field another goroutine reads".
findings.fix: Relocate the `select {}` line to the select edge-cases section on page 5 and the nil-a-local warning to the "Ownership" section, leaving "Guard Every Send" solely about ctx-guarded sends.
